[35] (Table 1): Weber’s length (WL); relative eye length (RelEL), calculated as the ratio of EL to WL; relative scape length (RelSL), calculated as the ratio of SL to WL; relative mandible length (RelML), the ratio of ML to WL; and relative hindleg length (RelHL), calculated as the sum of HFL and HTL, divided by WL.

Thus, the proposed justification for the use of eye size listed in Table 1 probably does not apply to subterranean species, and assigning a RelEL of 0 for these species may therefore mischaracterize the “functional position” of eyeless ants.

caste.quote: All worker ants were counted and identified to genus and then species or morphospecies by CJB and ZX.
A maximum of three worker ants per species were measured for each elevational band.
a species from Mengla (Dorylus laevigatus (Smith)) was removed because the only available specimens consisted of non-minor workers.

basisOfRecord.quote: Malaise trap—A Townes Malaise trap was set just outside each plot and operated for 10 days.
Pitfall traps—A total of 10 × 120 mL pitfall traps, each with an internal diameter of 44 mm and filled with 95% ethanol, were placed in each plot and left open for ten days.
Hand collection—At each plot, hand collections were performed once within the 50 m radius of the plot for one hour during the day (09:00–17:00 h).
A total of 1,165 individuals (Mengla: 995; Ailaoshan: 170) were measured and used for computing functional alpha and beta diversity.
